metadata.title: Identifying Emotional States using Keystroke Dynamics

abstract: The ability to recognize emotions is critical for building intelligent computers. Current emotion detection methods are invasive and require costly equipment. This paper proposes using keystroke dynamics to detect emotional states through typing patterns on standard keyboards. A field study collected keystroke data and self-reported emotional states, achieving 77-88% accuracy for six emotional states and 84% for anger and excitement.

research.problem: Current emotion detection systems are invasive and require specialized equipment.
research.motivation: Emotionally-aware systems can improve user interaction and adapt to contextual emotional states.
research.objective: Detect user emotional states using keystroke dynamics without intrusive hardware.

methodology.summary: Keystroke features (dwell time, flight time) were extracted from field study data using decision-tree classifiers for 15 emotional states.
datasets: Field study keystroke data with self-reported emotional states
preprocessing: Feature extraction from raw keystroke data
methodology.training_strategy: Classifier training using derived keystroke features

experiments.experimental_setup: Field study with experience-sampling methodology collecting keystrokes and emotional state self-reports.
experiments.results: Classifiers achieved 77.4-87.8% accuracy for confidence, hesitance, nervousness, relaxation, sadness, and tiredness; 84% for anger and excitement.

contributions: Non-intrusive emotion detection using standard keyboards
future_work: Test across diverse typing abilities and keyboards
analysis.research_gap: Need for more studies on emotional state variability and cross-context generalization

sections.introduction: Discusses usability challenges in interactive applications due to lack of emotional context awareness and proposes emotion-sensing systems.
sections.related_work: Reviews affective computing and keystroke dynamics, highlighting limitations of physiological sensors and intrusive methods.
sections.methodology: Describes field study design, keystroke feature extraction, and classifier development for emotional state detection.
sections.results: Presents accuracy metrics for 15 emotional states using keystroke dynamics classifiers.
sections.discussion: Analyzes implications of non-intrusive emotion sensing for human-computer interaction and system adaptability.
sections.conclusion: Emphasizes potential of keystroke dynamics for improving user experience through emotionally-aware systems.
